## Summary

Compare turnover metrics against biomass change.

## Data

* AquaX species distribution models from Reygondeau et al. (2026). AquaX: An enhanced and revised AquaMaps framework to model marine species distributions and biodiversity. PLOS ONE, 21(2), e0335823. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0335823
* Function entities from O'Hara et al. (2024). Cumulative human impacts on global marine fauna highlight risk to biological and functional diversity. PLOS ONE, 19(9), e0309788. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0309788
* Biomass projections from ISIMIP 3b

## Methods

* Rasterize the SPP and FE turnover maps
* Rasterize the biomass projection maps
* Ideas for potential zonal comparison:
    * Fisheries quartiles?
    * Turnover quartiles?
* Other ideas for comparison
    * Regression?
    * PCA?
* NOTE: should the quartile breakdowns be implemented using an equal area projection, to avoid overemphasizing arctic and antarctic regions at the expense of equatorial regions?
    * YES! we will be using the behrmann projection, equal area cylindrical

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(ggpattern)
library(here)
library(terra)
library(sf)
library(arrow)
library(collapse)
library(biscale)  ### for bivariate legend
library(cowplot)

source(here('common_fxns.R'))
```


### Load biomass projections

Biomass change ensemble model generated in scripts `map_biomass_change.qmd`.  These are already in raster format and Behrmann projection at 5 km resolution.  

Note, the "agreement" layer ranges from -6 to 6, representing the sum of signs of the ensemble model outputs.

* +/- 6: all six models are in same direction
* +/- 4: one model disagrees (e.g., 5+, 1- is +4)
* +/- 2, or 0: two or more models disagreeing

```{r biomass change}
biomass_r <- rast(here('_output/impact_maps/biomass_change_ssp585_2050.tif'))
biomass_r[[1]][biomass_r[[1]] > .4] <- .4 ### cap at +40% - only affects 0.003 of data

biomass_df <- as.data.frame(biomass_r, xy = TRUE)

### set up low-confidence polygons
lo_conf_r <- biomass_r[[3]]
lo_conf_r[abs(lo_conf_r) >= 4] <- NA
lo_conf_sf <- as.polygons(lo_conf_r, aggregate = TRUE, values = FALSE) |> 
  st_as_sf()
```

### Read in and rasterize turnover metrics

These rasters were created in scripts 3 (spp turnover) and 4 (fe turnover) in the Behrmann projection.

```{r read rasts}

spp_turn_r <- rast(here('_output/spp_turnover_maps/all_spp_turnover.tif'))
fe_turn_r  <- rast(here('_output/fe_turnover_maps/all_fe_turnover.tif'))

# plot(spp_turn_r); plot(fe_turn_r)
```

## Generate Manuscript Figures

### Map biomass including agreement

Use cross hatching to indicate moderate agreement (5 models), no crosshatching to indicate disagreement 

```{r}
### pal <- hcl.colors(n = 3, palette = 'Red-Green')
pal <- c("#841859", "#FFFFEE", "#005600")
### convenience function for putting crosshatching on maps
geom_lowconf_hash <- function() {
  list(geom_sf_pattern(data = lo_conf_sf, 
                  fill = NA, color = NA, ### hide sf lines
                  pattern = 'stripe',
                  pattern_fill = 'grey30',
                  pattern_color = NA,
                  pattern_angle = 30,
                  pattern_density = .1,
                  pattern_spacing = .02))
}

biomass_map <- plot_map(biomass_df, fill_var = mean_ssp585_2050) +
  geom_lowconf_hash() +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = pal[1], mid = pal[2], high = pal[3],
                       limits = c(-.4, .4),
                       breaks = c(-0.4, 0, 0.4), labels = c('-40%', '0', '≥+40%')) +
  guides(alpha = 'none', fill = 'none') +
  labs(fill = 'Biomass\nchange') +
  theme(text = element_text(family = 'Helvetica'))
 
biomass_map
```

### set up biomass change marginal legend

```{r create marginal color legend}
biomass_marg_plot <- plot_marginal(df = biomass_df,
                                   var = mean_ssp585_2050,
                                   data_range = c(-.4, .4))

biomass_marg_plot
```

### Map biomass vs turnover bivariate plot

Here let's do a bivariate plot to compare areas of reduced biomass to high/low projected turnover.

Keep turnover metrics in their original 0-1 values.  For FE, this means few if any cells in the top quartile since few if any locations have 75%-100% functional turnover.

For biomass reduction, let's bin as -40 to -25, -25 to -10, -10 to 0, 0+ (or similar).

```{r process to quartiles}
fe_turn_biomass_f  <- here('_output/figure_data/fig_fe_turnover_biomass.parquet')
spp_turn_biomass_f <- here('_output/figure_data/fig_spp_turnover_biomass.parquet')

if(any(!file.exists(c(fe_turn_biomass_f, spp_turn_biomass_f)))) {
  biomass_qtile <- biomass_r[[1]] |> 
    setNames('biomass_rcp85')
  fe_turn_qtile <- spp_turn_qtile <- spp_turn_r ### initialize three new maps

  ### Set breaks for biomass:
  # x <- values(biomass_qtile); quantile(x, c(.25, .5, .75))
  #          25%         50%         75% 
  #  -0.11225004 -0.06233479 -0.02017238 
  # quantile_fxn <- ecdf(x); quantile_fxn(c(-.10, -.05, 0))
  # [1] 0.3007701 0.5687596 0.8267221
  biomass_thresh <- c(-.4, -.1, -.05, 0)

  ### NOTE - setting so positive values --> 1, lowest negative --> 4
  values(biomass_qtile) <- data.table::fcase(values(biomass_qtile) <= biomass_thresh[2], 4L,
                                             values(biomass_qtile) <= biomass_thresh[3], 3L,
                                             values(biomass_qtile) <= biomass_thresh[4], 2L,
                                             !is.na(values(biomass_qtile)), 1L)

  ### Set breaks for turnover - use values, not quartiles
  # x <- values(spp_turn_r); quantile(x, c(.25, .5, .75), na.rm = TRUE)
  #       25%       50%       75% 
  # 0.2808638 0.3867612 0.5319232 
  # quantile_fxn <- ecdf(values(spp_turn_r)); quantile_fxn(c(.15, .25, .5))
  # [1] 0.06780601 0.18575249 0.70237057
  # quantile_fxn <- ecdf(values(fe_turn_r));  quantile_fxn(c(.15, .25, .5))
  # [1] 0.2892683 0.6515390 0.9699684

  set_turnover_breaks <- function(r, breaks = c(.15, .25, .5)) {
    v <- values(r) |> as.vector()
    x <- case_when(v < breaks[1] ~ 1,
                   v < breaks[2] ~ 2,
                   v < breaks[3] ~ 3,
                   !is.na(v) ~ 4,
                   TRUE ~ NA_integer_)
  }
  values(fe_turn_qtile)  <- set_turnover_breaks(fe_turn_r)
  values(spp_turn_qtile) <- set_turnover_breaks(spp_turn_r)

  fe_turn_biomass_df <- as.data.frame(c(fe_turn_qtile, biomass_qtile), xy = TRUE) %>%
    rename(fe_turn_rcp45 = rcp45_2050, fe_turn_rcp85 = rcp85_2050) %>%
    mutate(bi_class_rcp45 = paste(fe_turn_rcp45, biomass_rcp85, sep = '-'),
           bi_class_rcp85 = paste(fe_turn_rcp85, biomass_rcp85, sep = '-'))
  spp_turn_biomass_df <- as.data.frame(c(spp_turn_qtile, biomass_qtile), xy = TRUE) %>%
    rename(spp_turn_rcp45 = rcp45_2050, spp_turn_rcp85 = rcp85_2050) %>%
    mutate(bi_class_rcp45 = paste(spp_turn_rcp45, biomass_rcp85, sep = '-'),
           bi_class_rcp85 = paste(spp_turn_rcp85, biomass_rcp85, sep = '-'))

  write_parquet(fe_turn_biomass_df,  fe_turn_biomass_f)
  write_parquet(spp_turn_biomass_df, spp_turn_biomass_f)
}

fe_turn_biomass_df  <- read_parquet(fe_turn_biomass_f)
spp_turn_biomass_df <- read_parquet(spp_turn_biomass_f)

```

```{r set up biplot}
calc_biplot_pcts <- function(df, scenario = 'rcp45') {
  df_sum <- df %>% 
    select(bi_class = all_of(paste0('bi_class_', scenario))) %>%
    fsubset(!grepl('NA', bi_class)) %>%
    fcount(bi_class) %>%
    mutate(pct = N / sum(N)) %>%
    separate_wider_delim(bi_class, names = c('turn', 'biomass'), delim = '-') %>%
    mutate(turn = as.integer(turn), biomass = as.integer(biomass),
           lbl = paste0(round(pct, 3) * 100, '%'),
           dark = biomass >= 3 & turn >= 3)
}
fe_turn_pcts_rcp45 <- fe_turn_biomass_df %>%
  calc_biplot_pcts(scenario = 'rcp45')
spp_turn_pcts_rcp45 <- spp_turn_biomass_df %>%
  calc_biplot_pcts(scenario = 'rcp45')
```
```{r build palette}

map_pal_raw <- bi_pal(pal = 'GrPink2', dim = 4, preview = FALSE)
  
map_pal_mtx      <- matrix(map_pal_raw, nrow = 4, ncol = 4)
map_pal_mtx[3, ] <- colorspace::lighten(map_pal_mtx[3, ], .1)
map_pal_mtx[2, ] <- colorspace::lighten(map_pal_mtx[2, ], .2)
map_pal_mtx[1, ] <- colorspace::lighten(map_pal_mtx[1, ], .3)
map_pal_mtx[ , 3] <- colorspace::lighten(map_pal_mtx[ , 3], .1)
map_pal_mtx[ , 2] <- colorspace::lighten(map_pal_mtx[ , 2], .2)
map_pal_mtx[ , 1] <- colorspace::lighten(map_pal_mtx[ , 1], .3)
map_pal_mtx[1, 1] <- '#ffffee'

map_pal <- as.vector(map_pal_mtx) %>% setNames(names(map_pal_raw))

theme_legend <- function() {
  list(
    scale_color_manual(values = c('grey20', 'white')),
    theme(text = element_text(family = 'Helvetica'),
          axis.ticks.length = unit(0, 'cm'),
          axis.text  = element_text(size = 6),
          axis.title = element_text(size = 8),
          axis.text.x = element_text(margin = margin(t = 0)),
          axis.text.y = element_text(margin = margin(r = 0))),
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1, 2, 3, 4),
                       labels = c("[0, 15)", "[15, 25)", "[25, 50)", "[50, 100]"),
                       expand = c(0, 0)),
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(1, 2, 3, 4),
                       labels = c("gain", "[0, 5)",  "[5, 10)", "[10, 40]"),
                       expand = c(0, 0))
  )
}

pnl_lgd_fe <- bi_legend(pal = map_pal, dim = 4,
                        x = 'Functional turnover (%)',
                        y = 'Biomass decrease (%)') +
  geom_text(data = fe_turn_pcts_rcp45, 
            aes(x = turn, y = biomass, label = lbl, color = dark),
            family = 'Helvetica',
            size = 2.5, show.legend = FALSE) +
  theme_legend()


pnl_lgd_spp <- bi_legend(pal = map_pal, dim = 4,
                        x = 'Species turnover (%)',
                        y = 'Biomass decrease (%)') +
  geom_text(data = spp_turn_pcts_rcp45, 
            aes(x = turn, y = biomass, label = lbl, color = dark),
            family = 'Helvetica',
            size = 2.5, show.legend = FALSE) +
  theme_legend()
```

```{r fe_45}
  geom_lowconf_hash() +
  bi_scale_fill(pal = map_pal, dim = 4) +
  theme(axis.text = element_blank(), 
        axis.title = element_blank(),
        legend.position = 'none')

# panel_fe_45
```

#### Assemble turnover X biomass figure

Figure shows RCP4.5 spp and FE turnover vs. biomass.  Biomass are same, but FE turnover will be less than SPP turnover.

```{r pull panels}
# lgd_a <- get_legend(biomass_map)
lgd_b <- pnl_lgd_spp
lgd_c <- pnl_lgd_fe
pnl_a <- get_panel(biomass_map)
mrg_a <- get_panel(biomass_marg_plot)
pnl_b <- panel_spp_45
pnl_c <- panel_fe_45
```
